target.title: fix(codex): session permissions persist across resumed turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who changed Codex session permissions with `/codex permissions` would lose those approval and sandbox choices on later primary turns or after a gateway restart. It also makes the live Codex compaction stress test prove the exact native command result instead of accepting marker echoes, unrelated results, contradictory durable rows, or weak compaction evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stored session permissions now feed resumed primary harness connections unless explicit OpenClaw exec policy or supervision owns the connection. The stress harness uses one exact command identity across request-local events and durable history, accepts compaction fallback only when the exact result row is absent, keeps failure diagnostics bounded and redacted, and can launch the CLI from a clean source checkout without prebuilt dist output.

## User Impact

Codex permission changes now survive ordinary follow-up messages and gateway restarts. Maintainers get stricter, restart-capable large-output and compaction stress proof with fewer false passes.

## Evidence

- Focused gateway oracle: 58 tests passed.
- Focused Codex run-attempt lane: 116 tests passed.
- Fresh autoreview: clean; no accepted/actionable findings.
- Remote changed gate passed all four typecheck lanes, formatting, core/extensions/scripts lint, contract guards, import-cycle checks, and live Docker scheduler dry-run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29669805771
- Live GPT-5.6 Luna API-key gateway run passed image, MCP, Guardian, 12 subagents, 8 x 1 MB native outputs before restart, 20 history turns, 10 gateway/app-server restarts on the same thread, and another 8 x 1 MB outputs after restart: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29664068201
- A later strict rerun correctly failed when Codex emitted no automatic compaction after the large-output turns; the oracle was not weakened to manufacture a pass.

AI-assisted. I reviewed the implementation, upstream Codex contracts, live behavior, and generated evidence.
